title: Dietary Lipids Shape Neuroimmune Microenvironment in Alzheimer’s Disease: A Stage-Specific Framework for Precision Nutrition
content: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is no longer viewed simply as a proteinopathy driven by amyloid-β (Aβ) and tau. It also involves neuroimmune dysregulation, blood-brain barrier (BBB) and neurovascular unit (NVU) dysfunction, gut-brain axis perturbation, and peripheral metabolic imbalance. Dietary lipids are biologically distinct molecules that can influence these systems through membrane remodeling, lipid-mediator generation, receptor signaling, metabolic support, and central-peripheral crosstalk. Clinical studies of n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) and related lipid interventions have nevertheless produced inconsistent or negative results, which may reflect both genuinely limited efficacy in some settings and heterogeneity in lipid species, disease stage, formulation, exposure, and host background. We therefore place the proposed 4D framework within a broader systems-physiology concept of allostatic integrity: the capacity of interacting neural, glial, vascular, immune, and metabolic systems to adapt to repeated perturbations and return toward functional stability. We further use “biological memory” as an operational concept for persistent molecular and cellular state changes—such as epigenetic, metabolic, lipidomic, and glial-state remodeling—that can alter responses to subsequent challenges. The 4D framework comprises Disease stage, Dominant driver pathway, Delivery and formulation, and Data-guided stratification. It is intended as a hypothesis-generating research framework for trial design and stratification, not as a validated clinical algorithm. The 4D framework has not yet been prospectively validated, and its prospective utility remains to be tested.
